features.description: When Markie's embedded terminal is enabled, a new shell starts in the current document folder and exposes MARKIE_FILE, MARKIE_DIR, and MARKIE_WORKSPACE for the active document.
steps: Open a markdown file in Markie with the terminal feature enabled in a development run.
Create a new embedded terminal session.
Run `pwd` and confirm it starts in the active document's folder.
Run `printf '%s\n' "$MARKIE_FILE" "$MARKIE_DIR" "$MARKIE_WORKSPACE"` and confirm the values match the active document and workspace.
Run the focused terminal regression test plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm test -- electron/terminal.test.ts` passed with 5 tests, including terminal Markie context regression. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-015021-post-f001.log 2>&1` passed renderer tests, MCP tests, server tests, lint, and build.
features.notes: Implemented env/cwd injection only. The terminal UI remains hidden by `TERMINAL_ENABLED = false`, so the user journey was verified via the focused Electron terminal regression instead of manual UI driving.

features.description: When the active document changes, future embedded terminal sessions receive updated Markie context instead of stale document paths.
steps: Open document A, then open document B in the same Markie session.
Create a new embedded terminal session after document B becomes active.
Confirm MARKIE_FILE and MARKIE_DIR point at document B, not document A.
Run the focused terminal regression test plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm test -- electron/terminal.test.ts` passed with 6 tests, including the document A to document B future-shell context regression. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-automated-f002-post.log 2>&1` passed renderer tests, MCP tests, server tests, lint, and build.
features.notes: Depends on F-001. Verified future shells pick up the newly active document context. Existing shells are intentionally not re-injected.

features.description: A safe preflight command verifies release prerequisites without signing, notarizing, uploading, or touching production services.
steps: Run the documented release preflight command on a clean checkout without release credentials.
Confirm it checks package metadata, required local files, and build/test prerequisites.
Confirm it exits before any publish, notarize, upload, deploy, or credentialed network action.
Run `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm test -- electron/release-preflight.test.ts` passed 3 tests. `npm run release:preflight > .autoloop/runs/release-preflight-20260628-035123.log 2>&1` passed metadata, required-file, renderer/Electron, MCP, server, lint, and static build checks, ending before credentialed release actions. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-035139-post-f003.log 2>&1` passed.
features.notes: Added `npm run release:preflight` as a local-only DX gate. Actual signing, notarization, upload, publish, deploy, and credentialed release actions remain human checkpoints.

features.description: The MCP server has a regression journey proving allowed markdown writes remain fenced to safe local markdown paths.
steps: Run the MCP test suite and identify the current filesystem guard coverage.
Add a user-observable MCP write/read regression that writes an allowed markdown file under a temporary safe home and reads it back.
Confirm symlink escape and unsafe extension cases still fail.
Run `node --test mcp/lib.test.mjs` and `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `node --test mcp/lib.test.mjs > .autoloop/runs/mcp-lib-f004-20260628.log 2>&1` passed 15 tests, including a stdio MCP `markie_write_md`/`markie_read_md` journey under a temporary safe home plus unsafe extension and symlink escape tool-level failures. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-automated-f004-post.log 2>&1` passed renderer tests, MCP tests, server tests, lint, and build.
features.notes: Did not widen the MCP public API shape; added regression coverage through the existing JSON-RPC `tools/call` path.

features.description: A real-user comments regression verifies thread creation, reply, resolve, reopen, and anchor survival using the existing verifier scripts.
steps: Run the existing comments verification scripts against the local dev server setup they document.
If setup gaps prevent the journey, add the smallest script/docs fix needed for repeatable local verification.
Confirm the journey covers create, reply, resolve, reopen, and anchor survival after an edit above the selection.
Run the focused comments verifier plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm run comments:verify:e2e > .autoloop/runs/comments-verify-e2e-20260628.log 2>&1` passed. The wrapper ran the comments API verifier from a migrated temp DB and the Electron/CDP UI verifier, covering create, reply, resolve, reopen, and Yjs anchor survival after Bob inserted content above Alice's selection.
features.notes: Added repeatable local verifier orchestration and an E2E-only Electron launch escape hatch; comments product UX was unchanged.

features.description: A repeatable light-mode visual audit captures the primary Markie app shell and flags invisible or low-contrast UI before style fixes continue.
steps: Start the app or renderer in a local development environment with the built-in light theme active.
Capture screenshots or DOM/computed-style evidence for the toolbar, editor/rich view, left rail, library, command palette, settings, share dialog, and comments surfaces.
Record each invisible or low-contrast issue as a concrete checklist in a local audit artifact or test output.
Run the focused audit plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm run visual:audit:light > .autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-20260628-focused.log 2>&1` passed and wrote `.autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-20260628150614/audit.json` plus screenshots for shell, PDF menu, Library probe, command palette, settings probe, and share/comments probes. The audit recorded 3 concrete light-mode contrast findings: PDF menu options at 2.2:1 and markdown strong text at 1.04:1. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-f006-post.log 2>&1` passed.
features.notes: Audit/harness/evidence only. The findings map to the existing follow-up scopes: F-007 for toolbar/PDF menu contrast and F-010 for markdown strong text/content contrast.

features.description: Light mode is legible in the top toolbar, mode switcher, PDF/export menu, file controls, and activity/header chrome.
steps: Use the light-mode audit evidence from F-006 to identify toolbar/header/menu contrast failures.
Replace hardcoded dark styles and weak token combinations with theme-aware colors for that surface only.
Verify toolbar controls, hover/active states, dropdown text, dividers, and disabled/secondary text are visible in light and dark mode.
Run the focused style check or screenshot comparison plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm run visual:audit:light > .autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-f007-20260628.log 2>&1` passed and wrote `.autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-20260628155223/audit.json` plus screenshots. Toolbar, file control, and PDF menu samples passed AA contrast in light mode; PDF menu options improved from 2.2:1 to 6.38:1. `npm test -- src/lib/theme.test.ts > .autoloop/runs/theme-test-f007-20260628.log 2>&1` passed 6 tests, including built-in dark/light top-chrome token contrast. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-f007-post.log 2>&1` passed.
features.notes: Fixed top chrome only by removing the hardcoded dark PDF menu background and keeping the audit probe on theme tokens. The remaining editor strong-text light-mode finding stays reserved for F-010.

features.description: Light mode is legible in side-panel surfaces: Library, Browse, Skills/Agents, Shared, and file lists.
steps: Inspect side-panel surfaces in light and dark mode using the established audit harness.
Fix invisible links, badges, rows, empty states, buttons, and selected/hover states in the side panels.
Verify side panels remain readable at narrow and normal desktop widths.
Run the focused visual/style verification plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm run visual:audit:light > .autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-f008-20260628.log 2>&1` passed and wrote `.autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-20260628170137/audit.json`; `sidePanelFindings` is empty and Library/Browse/Files/Shared/Skills side-panel samples pass AA in light mode, including normal and narrow screenshots. `npm test -- src/lib/color-mode.test.ts src/lib/theme.test.ts > .autoloop/runs/theme-tests-f008-20260628.log 2>&1` passed 9 tests, including root dark-class toggling and built-in side-panel status color contrast. Browser sanity on http://localhost:3000 loaded Markie, opened Library, and reported zero console warnings/errors. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-f008-post.log 2>&1` passed renderer tests, MCP tests, server tests, lint, and build.
features.notes: Fixed side-panel theme semantics only. Status badges/actions and starred states now use active-theme CSS variables instead of dark-biased Tailwind color variants; the audit still records the known editor strong-text finding reserved for F-010.

features.description: Light mode is legible in modal and popover surfaces: command palette, settings, theme settings, stats, share, agents, and comments.
steps: Open each modal/popover surface in light and dark mode.
Fix hardcoded dark backgrounds, invisible text, weak borders, and unreadable hover/focus states in those surfaces.
Verify keyboard focus visibility and text contrast for each modal/popover.
Run the focused visual/style verification plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm run visual:audit:light > .autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-f009-20260628.log 2>&1` passed and wrote `.autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-20260628175435/audit.json` plus screenshots. Newly sampled command palette, settings, theme settings, stats, share, agents, and comments overlay targets all passed AA contrast in built-in light mode; share/comment status colors measured 5.88:1 to 6.86:1 and the stats popover measured 6.38:1 to 14.62:1. `npm test -- src/lib/theme.test.ts > .autoloop/runs/theme-test-f009-20260628.log 2>&1` passed 7 tests. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-f009-post.log 2>&1` passed renderer tests, MCP tests, server tests, lint, and build.
features.notes: Fixed overlay-only theme-token issues: the stats popover and table bar no longer hardcode a dark surface, and overlay success/error/warning/resolved/delete text now uses built-in status tokens. The audit still records the known editor strong-text finding reserved for F-010.

features.description: Markdown and rich editor content use theme-aware colors so light mode does not hide strong text, inline code, code blocks, tables, selections, or task controls.
steps: Open a document containing headings, bold text, links, inline code, code blocks, tables, task lists, blockquotes, math, and comments in light and dark mode.
Fix hardcoded content colors and highlight styles that make content invisible or visually broken in light mode.
Add or update theme/content tests where pure style-token behavior is testable.
Run the focused content-style verification plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm run visual:audit:light > .autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-f010-20260628.log 2>&1` passed and wrote `.autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-20260628185757/audit.json` plus screenshots; `contentFindings` is empty and editor content samples pass AA contrast in built-in light mode, including strong text at 16.97:1, links at 4.95:1, inline code at 6.29:1, code blocks at 15.71:1, blockquotes at 6.85:1, checked task controls at 4.95:1, tables, headings, and math text. `npm test -- src/lib/theme.test.ts > .autoloop/runs/theme-test-f010-20260628.log 2>&1` passed 8 tests covering built-in dark/light document token contrast. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-f010-post.log 2>&1` passed.
features.notes: Fixed document content only: strong text, inline code, and checked task controls now use active theme tokens. Expanded the default sample and audit coverage so links, inline code, code blocks, tables, blockquotes, task controls, and math text remain observable.

features.description: A visual regression guard prevents future built-in theme contrast regressions across representative Markie surfaces.
steps: Turn the light-mode audit/fix workflow into a repeatable test or script that can run headlessly or with a local app window.
Cover at least one representative shell surface, one editor/content surface, and one modal/panel surface.
Make the script fail or produce clear findings when key foreground/background pairs fall below the chosen contrast threshold.
Run the visual regression guard plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm run visual:guard:theme > .autoloop/runs/theme-visual-guard-f011-20260628-final.log 2>&1` passed and wrote `.autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-20260628195511/audit.json` plus screenshots. The guard sampled 6 shell, 11 content, and 16 overlay/panel targets at a 4.5 AA threshold with zero findings; checked task controls measured 4.95:1 after the live ProseMirror checkbox override. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-f011-post.log 2>&1` passed.
features.notes: Added `npm run visual:guard:theme` as a dependency-free regression guard around the existing audit. The regular audit still writes findings/artifacts; guard mode fails when required shell, content, or overlay/panel samples are missing or below AA contrast.

features.description: The primary desktop shell receives one native-feeling refinement pass for spacing, density, window chrome, and panel boundaries.
steps: Review the main app shell after light-mode fixes in both light and dark mode.
Make a narrow layout polish pass on toolbar height/density, rail alignment, panel borders, and content spacing without changing navigation structure.
Verify no text overlaps or clips at the minimum supported window size and at a normal desktop size.
Run screenshot/visual verification plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: In-app browser QA against `http://localhost:3002/` passed with zero console warnings/errors and wrote `.autoloop/runs/shell-layout-browser-f012-20260628.json`; normal dark mode measured a 40px toolbar, 48px rail, 1188px document area, and no sampled overflow, while compact 760x720 dark and light modes both measured no sampled overflow after clicking the real Light theme toolbar control. `npm run visual:guard:theme > .autoloop/runs/theme-visual-guard-f012-20260628-rerun.log 2>&1` passed and wrote `.autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-20260628210028/audit.json` plus shell, PDF menu, library, narrow side-panel, command palette, settings, and gated surface screenshots with zero findings. `npm test -- src/lib/theme.test.ts src/lib/color-mode.test.ts > .autoloop/runs/theme-tests-f012-20260628.log 2>&1` passed. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-f012-post.log 2>&1` passed.
features.notes: Completed one narrow shell polish pass: denser native-feeling toolbar/rail, clearer side-panel boundaries, responsive document/source spacing, and a visual audit harness that avoids unrelated port-3000 dev servers.

features.description: The editor and document canvas receive one refinement pass for reading width, split-mode balance, empty states, and responsive behavior.
steps: Inspect editor, rich view, preview, split mode, and empty/welcome states at narrow and normal desktop widths.
Make one focused layout refinement pass that improves native polish without changing core editor behavior.
Verify long filenames, long headings, and common markdown examples do not overlap or clip.
Run screenshot/visual verification plus `./init.sh`.
features.evidence: `npm run visual:check:document > .autoloop/runs/document-layout-check-f013-20260628-final.log 2>&1` passed and wrote `.autoloop/runs/document-layout-check-20260628215931/document-layout.json` plus screenshots for normal preview, normal split, compact split, compact edit, and compact empty states. The final metrics reported zero document-node overflows, no source/rich pane overlap, 0px split gaps, bounded rich canvases, and usable source/rich pane widths. `npm run visual:guard:theme > .autoloop/runs/theme-visual-guard-f013-20260628.log 2>&1` passed with zero findings across shell/content/overlay samples and wrote `.autoloop/runs/light-mode-audit-20260628215943/audit.json`. `./init.sh > .autoloop/runs/init-20260628-f013-post.log 2>&1` passed.
features.notes: Completed one focused document work-area polish pass: single-pane View/Edit now fill the canvas, split mode uses an explicit grid balance, rich content stays bounded to the theme reading width, and long headings/common markdown wrap or scroll inside the document area.

features.description: Keyboard-first overlays and menus receive one native-feeling refinement pass for focus, hover, spacing, and hierarchy.
steps: Inspect command palette, menus, settings, share, stats, and theme settings after the light-mode overlay fixes.
Make one focused polish pass that improves focus rings, menu spacing, hierarchy, and native-feeling affordances.
Verify keyboard navigation and focus visibility still work.
Run focused interaction/visual verification plus `./init.sh`.
features.notes: Do not add new feature surface; polish existing overlays.

features.description: A cross-platform desktop audit maps macOS-only assumptions and creates a safe implementation checklist for Windows, Intel Mac, and Linux support.
steps: Search Electron, renderer, MCP, release, and docs code for macOS-only assumptions and Apple-Silicon-only release assumptions.
Classify each finding as runtime behavior, packaging config, docs/download page, test/preflight, or human-gated release/deploy work.
Add the resulting checklist to the roadmap docs or backlog without changing runtime behavior.
Run `./init.sh`.
features.notes: Start cross-platform work with a map. Do not publish or deploy.

features.description: Markie's runtime gracefully handles non-macOS platforms for platform-specific actions instead of assuming Darwin behavior.
steps: Use the F-015 audit to pick the highest-impact runtime macOS assumption that can be fixed without API redesign.
Add or update tests for darwin, win32, linux, and unsupported/fallback branches.
Implement the smallest runtime guard or platform abstraction for that action.
Run the focused platform test plus `./init.sh`.
features.notes: One platform behavior per wakeup. Add follow-up ledger items for additional assumptions discovered.

features.description: Electron packaging config supports local dry-run targets for Apple Silicon macOS, Intel macOS, Windows, and Linux without publishing.
steps: Inspect existing electron-builder configuration and release docs.
Add or adjust local-only packaging scripts/config for mac arm64, mac x64, Windows, and Linux targets while keeping publish disabled by default.
Verify the config can be parsed and the safe local packaging/preflight command stops before signing, notarization, upload, publish, or deploy.
Run the packaging/preflight verification plus `./init.sh`.
features.notes: No publishing. If cross-compilation cannot build an artifact on the current host, the task should still add a verifiable dry-run/preflight.

features.description: Release docs and local preflight describe how to produce and verify downloads for macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, Windows, and Linux.
steps: Update release documentation to include per-platform artifact names, local build commands, signing/notarization expectations, and verification steps.
Update the local release preflight to validate required metadata for all desktop platforms without requiring credentials.
Verify the docs and preflight make it impossible to confuse local dry-run checks with actual publishing.
Run the release preflight plus `./init.sh`.
features.notes: Keep actual signing, notarization, upload, and release as human checkpoints.

features.description: A download manifest or equivalent source of truth lists all supported desktop platform downloads for the download page.
steps: Find where the Markie download page is sourced from in this repo or document that it lives outside this repo.
Add a repo-local download manifest or documented interface covering Apple Silicon Mac, Intel Mac, Windows, and Linux artifact labels, filenames, and URLs/placeholders.
Add a test or validation script that checks the manifest shape and required platform entries.
Run the manifest validation plus `./init.sh`.
features.notes: Do not deploy the page. If the live marketing site is in another repo, leave an explicit integration note and keep the manifest here.

features.description: The download page or public-facing download copy is updated to present all supported desktop platforms when the source lives in this repo.
steps: Use the F-019 manifest/source discovery to determine whether this repo owns the download page or only docs/metadata.
If this repo owns the page, update it to show Apple Silicon Mac, Intel Mac, Windows, and Linux downloads clearly.
If this repo does not own the page, update README/docs with the manifest contract and add a backlog item for the owning repo.
Run the relevant page/docs validation plus `./init.sh`.
features.notes: No production deploy. This task is complete when the repo-owned source or integration contract is updated and verified.

features.description: A React Native feasibility ADR defines the mobile product scope, shared-code strategy, and decisions that require human approval before scaffolding.
steps: Review current Electron/Next renderer, markdown pipeline, theme tokens, sync/auth client boundaries, and platform-specific Electron APIs.
Write an ADR for the React Native direction, including target platforms, MVP scope, shared modules, dependencies, and risks.
Explicitly list the stack/dependency decisions that require human approval before creating a React Native app.
Run `./init.sh`.
features.notes: Planning only. Do not scaffold React Native or add dependencies in this task.

features.description: Portable markdown/theme code boundaries are prepared so a future React Native app can reuse non-Electron logic.
steps: Use the React Native ADR to identify one pure module boundary that can be shared without adding a new app stack.
Extract or document that boundary while preserving existing Electron/Next behavior.
Add focused tests proving the shared pure logic still works.
Run the focused test plus `./init.sh`.
features.notes: No React Native dependencies. One pure-code boundary per wakeup; add follow-up items for additional boundaries.
